info.title: notefeed API
info.description:
Post markdown notes to a feed, read them back. See https://docs.notefeed.me/

Every error is JSON, `{"error": "...", "code": "..."}`. Besides the responses listed per operation, an unknown path under /api/v1 answers 404 (`not_found`) and a method an operation doesn't have answers 405 with `Allow`.

tags.name: Feeds
tags.description: By the feed's name, the write key. Need the instance password when one is set.

tags.name: Read
tags.description: By the feed's read id. Public and read-only.

tags.name: Licenses
tags.description: Where licenses are sold: what they cost, where to buy them and where buyers manage them. Public.

post.description: The body is the note, a file, and `Content-Type` says which kind: `text/markdown` (UTF-8, at most 102400 bytes), or an image, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif` or `image/webp` (at most NOTEFEED_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES as sent, default 10 MiB). Nothing is guessed: any other type, or none, is `415`, and so is a body that is not what the type says (an image is recognized by its first bytes; SVG is refused). Markdown is stored byte for byte. An image is stored processed, not as sent: turned the way its EXIF orientation says, scaled to at most 2560 px on its long side, encoded again in its own format (JPEG and WebP at quality 85, PNG lossless, an animated GIF or WebP keeps its frames), and without metadata (EXIF, GPS position, XMP, comments). Send it full size; one of more than 100 megapixels is `413`, and a body that does not decode as the image it declares is `415`. Creates the feed with its first note, optionally protected by its own password (`X-Feed-Password`; 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space at the start or end) and with the read id in `X-Read-Id`; both are only used by the post that creates the feed. Where licenses are sold, the post that creates the feed can bring a license key in `X-License-Key`, with or without a password; a feed password needs one, or the post is refused with `402`. Posting to a protected feed needs its password. Also served at `POST /{feed}`, the short form curl one-liners use. The response names the note's `file` and where it is served, `file_url`, under the feed's read id (public like the read link). Metadata goes in headers: `X-Note-Title`, `X-Note-Tags` (at most 10 tags, each 1 to 32 characters of letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`; case is folded to lowercase, duplicates are removed), `X-Note-Alt` (images), `X-Note-Name` (the original file name), `X-Note-Date` (where it is placed in the feed: a past date backdates it, a future one schedules it), `X-Note-Draft` (`true`: a draft, which readers do not see until it is published). A markdown note with its pictures is one `multipart/form-data` request: a `text` part (the markdown, a field or a file part; a file part keeps its line breaks, a field's are sent as CRLF), `file` parts (up to 10 pictures, each with its file name and image `Content-Type`) and `alt.<file name>` fields. The pictures are stored first, each as its own note named by its file name, then the text with its references to them (`![](chart.png)`, `[x]: chart.png`, as written or percent-decoded) swapped for the stored files; a picture it never refers to is appended as `![](file)`. Several pictures may have the same file name (a phone calls every photo `image.jpg`): each is stored, and they are appended, but a text that refers to such a name is 400. Everything is checked before the first write, and a failed write removes what the request stored: all or nothing. `X-Note-Alt` and `X-Note-Name` are 400. The answer has `attachments`, the stored pictures in the order of the `file` parts. The `text` part is optional: `X-Note-Title` goes on the text note, `X-Note-Tags` on every note, `X-Note-Date` on the text note (its pictures take the milliseconds just before it); with no `text` part only the pictures are stored, each with the title, and the answer's top level is the first picture. A refused multipart post that would have created a protected feed creates nothing.

parameters.name: feed
parameters.description: The feed's name. It is the write key: anyone who knows it can post.

parameters.name: X-Feed-Password
parameters.description: The feed's own password, when it has one: to post, list or get, and (as the current password) to change or remove it. On the `POST` that creates a feed it sets the feed's password; on a `POST` to an existing feed that has none it answers 409. An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

parameters.name: X-Read-Id
parameters.description: The read id the feed gets when this post creates it: 3 to 64 characters (a-z, 0-9, - and _), random when left out or empty, ignored for a feed that exists. A short readable one is guessable: protect the feed with a password if that matters. 409 when it is taken

parameters.name: X-License-Key
parameters.description: Only on an instance that sells licenses, on the post that creates the feed: the key of the license to put on the new feed, with or without `X-Feed-Password` (a feed password is for licensed feeds: with one and no key, 402). 400 for a key that is none, 402 for one whose license has lapsed; either way nothing is created. Ignored on an existing feed: put a license on it with `PUT /api/v1/feeds/{feed}/license`

parameters.name: X-Note-Title
parameters.description: The note's title, for a raw body; a JSON or form body's own `title` wins. At most 100 characters, one line, with no control or text-direction override characters.

parameters.name: X-Note-Tags
parameters.description: Tags for the note, comma-separated (`ci,deploy`): at most 10 tags, each 1 to 32 characters of letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`; case is folded to lowercase, duplicates are removed. For a raw markdown body; a JSON or form body's own `tags` wins. Empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Alt
parameters.description: For an image body: its alternative text; a form's own `alt` wins.

parameters.name: X-Note-Name
parameters.description: The note's file name (at most 200 characters; `/`, `\` and control characters are dropped): for a picture, its original name. The read link serves the newest note with that name at `/r/{readId}/{name}`, a stable address for a file that changes (a name ending in a lower-case extension, such as `post-to-notefeed.md`); a note's own file name (`<id>.<ext>`) comes first

parameters.name: X-Note-Date
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 date and time with its offset (`2026-10-01T09:30:00Z`, `2026-10-01T11:30:00+02:00`) or a date alone (midnight UTC). When the note is placed in the feed, from 1970 to 9999. A time after now schedules it: readers see it from then on. Empty is now.

parameters.name: X-Note-Draft
parameters.description: `true` stores the note, and its pictures, as a draft: only whoever can post to the feed sees it, readers do not until it is published. Left out or `false`: published

put.description: The body is the new file, with the same rules as posting: a `Content-Type` that is one of the accepted types, a body that is what it declares. A note keeps its type, so the type must be the note's own (`415` otherwise). An image is stored processed, not as sent: turned the way its EXIF orientation says, scaled to at most 2560 px on its long side, encoded again in its own format (JPEG and WebP at quality 85, PNG lossless, an animated GIF or WebP keeps its frames), and without metadata (EXIF, GPS position, XMP, comments). Send it full size; one of more than 100 megapixels is `413`, and a body that does not decode as the image it declares is `415`. Id, creation time and metadata stay: the title of a markdown note without one set follows the new text. Change the title, alt text or tags with `PATCH`. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Read links can't edit. A markdown note with its pictures is one `multipart/form-data` request: a `text` part (the markdown, a field or a file part; a file part keeps its line breaks, a field's are sent as CRLF), `file` parts (up to 10 pictures, each with its file name and image `Content-Type`) and `alt.<file name>` fields. The pictures are stored first, each as its own note named by its file name, then the text with its references to them (`![](chart.png)`, `[x]: chart.png`, as written or percent-decoded) swapped for the stored files; a picture it never refers to is appended as `![](file)`. Several pictures may have the same file name (a phone calls every photo `image.jpg`): each is stored, and they are appended, but a text that refers to such a name is 400. Everything is checked before the first write, and a failed write removes what the request stored: all or nothing. `X-Note-Alt` and `X-Note-Name` are 400. The answer has `attachments`, the stored pictures in the order of the `file` parts. On a `PUT` the `text` part is required and the note must be a markdown note; the note keeps its own title and tags, `X-Note-Tags` goes on the new pictures. A raw body ignores `X-Note-Tags`. The note is looked up first: a missing note is `404` and an image note `415` whatever the body holds.

patch.summary: Change a note's title, alt text, tags or date
patch.description: Sets the note's title, alt text (only for images), tags and/or date. An empty title or alt removes it: a markdown note's title follows its text again. `tags` replaces the whole list (an empty list removes them), with the same rules as on a post. A new date moves the note in the feed, with its attachments; a date after now schedules it. Id and links stay, and so does its RSS item's guid. At least one is needed. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Read links can't change notes.

post.summary: Create a feed without posting a note
post.description: Reserves the feed name now (ADR 0047): with a password it is protected from its first moment, with a read id it gets that read link. Where licenses are sold a license key is required and goes on the new feed; free feeds start with their first note. A feed that exists is 409. Counts against the post rate limit and the instance's feed cap, like a first post. After it, change the title and description with updateFeed.

put.description: Replaces both the title (at most 100 characters) and the description (at most 500); surrounding whitespace is trimmed and control and text-direction override characters are refused. `show_sender` (default true) shows who posted each note to readers; omitted leaves it as it is. `read_id` gives the feed another read link (3 to 64 characters: a-z, 0-9, - and _; empty for a random one): the old id is freed and answers like an unknown read id until another feed takes it, and the notes are not edited (a relative image link follows the new id, a full URL does not). A short readable read id is guessable, so protect the feed with a password if that matters. An instance can turn chosen read ids off (NOTEFEED_ALLOW_CUSTOM_IDS=0): then only an empty `read_id` is accepted. `image` is the file name `uploadImage` returned for this feed (title image), empty to remove it, or omitted to leave it as it is; any other value is a 400. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Only on a feed that exists: it is created by its first note. Read links can't change settings.

An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

put.description: On a protected feed: changes the password, with the current one in `X-Feed-Password`. On an open feed: sets one, with no current password, for whoever calls it. An open feed's name is all that protects it, so whoever knows the name may claim the feed this way. From then on everyone who posts to the feed, reads it by its name or changes it needs the password; the read link and RSS stay open.

A key notefeed doesn't know is 400 and counts as a failed attempt, like a wrong password. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. A license lifts a feed's free tier; a person buys it on `buy_url` and gets a key to put on a feed. Cancelling, the payment method and invoices are at the payment provider, where buyers sign in with the e-mail address they bought with (`manage_url`); no license key opens it (ADR 0050).
